request.theme: late night noir jazz for relaxation
request.admission: Every generated piece remains a candidate; the human decides admission later.

plan.albumMind: A sequence of self-contained nocturnal jazz studies where relaxation comes from unhurried pulse, spacious voicings, and gentle repetition, while noir character emerges through unresolved color, low-register counterlines, and restrained melodic shadows. Each piece offers a different way to settle: some through drifting piano, some through brushed ensemble motion, some through bass-led stillness, yet every ending feels deliberately softened rather than abruptly concluded.
plan.cohesionStrategy: Keep a restrained late-night dynamic ceiling, instrumental-only writing, nuanced swing or slow pulse, and jazz harmony colored by extensions, suspended tones, and selective chromaticism. Vary the foreground instrument, groove density, ensemble size, room perspective, harmonic rhythm, and degree of motivic activity in small groups: intimate piano-centered tracks, bass-and-brush meditations, and darker ensemble sketches. This creates contrast without breaking the relaxation arc; noir comes from harmonic ambiguity and register, not from loud drama.
plan.sharedSoundContract: Instrumental only, no vocals. Late-night noir jazz for relaxation: restrained dynamics, spacious phrasing, tactile acoustic playing, and jazz harmony with tasteful extensions, suspensions, and gentle chromatic tension. Every piece must have a clear self-contained arc, quiet entrance, gradual development, and softened ending. Vary foreground instrument, ensemble size, room intimacy, groove density, and harmonic rhythm, but avoid abrupt drops, flashy virtuosity, harsh brightness, or cinematic bombast.

tracks.title: Windowlight Waltz
tracks.musicalRole: Piano states a simple nocturnal motif while bass and brushes provide a floating three-beat cushion; the trio gradually trades fragments before returning to the motif.
tracks.groove: Slow, lightly swung 3/4 with flexible brush circles and understated bass anticipation.
tracks.harmony: Minor-colored tonic with added ninths, suspended dominants, and occasional chromatic passing chords; moderate harmonic rhythm.
tracks.development: Begin nearly solo, add bass and brushes after the first phrase, widen the piano voicings through a quiet middle passage, then thin back to piano and a final incomplete cadence.

tracks.title: Blue Smoke Ledger
tracks.musicalRole: Muted trumpet carries a sparse, descending theme while piano supplies dark intervallic punctuation and bass anchors the pauses.
tracks.groove: Unhurried 4/4, behind-the-beat swing with long rests and minimal cymbal activity.
tracks.harmony: Minor blues language without a fixed twelve-bar repetition; altered dominants resolve obliquely into major-sixth and minor-ninth colors.
tracks.development: Introduce the trumpet in isolated phrases, let piano answer with shorter figures, intensify through denser call-and-response, then dissolve into a final low trumpet breath and bass note.

tracks.title: Rain on the Fire Escape
tracks.musicalRole: Electric piano creates a repeating nocturnal ostinato while vibraphone and bass paint quiet reflections above it.
tracks.groove: Slow, even 6/8 with a gentle lilt and nearly continuous soft subdivision.
tracks.harmony: Bitonal upper structures over a stable minor bass center, resolving only partially through open fourths and added-sixth chords.
tracks.development: Establish the ostinato alone, introduce vibraphone as widely spaced replies, allow overlapping bell tones to thicken the center, then remove notes until the ostinato fades.

tracks.title: The Empty Booth
tracks.musicalRole: Solo piano alternates between a low walking suggestion and fragile treble commentary, making silence part of the phrasing.
tracks.groove: Free rubato with an implied slow swing, never fully settling into a metronomic pulse.
tracks.harmony: Sparse minor-major sonorities, planed fourths, and unresolved dominant colors; very slow harmonic rhythm.
tracks.development: Open with isolated low intervals, gradually form a recurring two-part gesture, briefly reach a more consonant register, then leave the final phrase suspended.

tracks.title: Streetlamp Half-Time
tracks.musicalRole: Bass and drums establish a calm half-time pocket while tenor saxophone develops a compact motif through repeated, slightly altered statements.
tracks.groove: Laid-back half-time swing, with bass phrases extending across the bar line and gentle mallet accents.
tracks.harmony: Dark modal vamp broadened by passing ii chords and restrained tritone substitutions; harmonic motion is cyclical rather than goal-driven.
tracks.development: Start with bass and sparse drum texture, bring in the saxophone motif, add electric-piano responses in the second cycle, then reduce to bass, breathy sax fragments, and a quiet vamp ending.

tracks.title: Nocturne for Closed Curtains
tracks.musicalRole: Clarinet and piano share a breath-like melody in imitation while cello supplies sustained shadow tones.
tracks.groove: Slow, pulse-based 4/4 with barely audible hand-drum emphasis and generous rubato at phrase endings.
tracks.harmony: Modal minor with pedal tones, parallel sixths, and delayed resolutions that keep the center veiled.
tracks.development: Piano presents the motif, bass clarinet echoes it lower, cello gradually lengthens the harmonic sustain, and the ensemble contracts into a final unison whisper.

tracks.title: Last Train, Softly
tracks.musicalRole: A brushed quartet maintains a quiet forward motion while guitar and saxophone exchange short motifs rather than taking extended solos.
tracks.groove: Gentle medium-slow swing with a discreet walking bass and softened ride texture.
tracks.harmony: Lyrical major-minor interchange, secondary dominants, and chromatic mediant turns that brighten briefly without becoming cheerful.
tracks.development: Guitar introduces a four-note cell, alto sax reshapes it in longer phrases, the bass briefly takes the foreground, and the group settles into a smaller final statement.

tracks.title: Ashes in the Blue Hour
tracks.musicalRole: Baritone saxophone provides low, sustained counterlines beneath sparse piano chords, creating weight without volume.
tracks.groove: Slow 12/8 blues pulse with brushed triplets and broad, breathing spaces.
tracks.harmony: Blues-derived minor harmony with flat-five coloration, suspended dominants, and long pedal-point passages.
tracks.development: Begin with piano and distant baritone, let bass join as a quiet anchor, build to overlapping low-register lines, then strip away the rhythm section for a hushed final chord.

tracks.title: Neon Herbarium
tracks.musicalRole: Vibraphone carries a delicate repeating melody while flugelhorn and piano alter its contour through understated replies.
tracks.groove: Relaxed straight-eighth pulse with soft syncopation and no pronounced backbeat.
tracks.harmony: Open quartal voicings over shifting bass notes, with occasional minor-second friction resolving into transparent sixths.
tracks.development: Present the vibraphone figure alone, add flugelhorn in long tones, let piano introduce counter-rhythms, then remove layers in reverse order while the figure slows and fades.

tracks.title: Velvet Corridor
tracks.musicalRole: Piano and guitar interlock a quiet chordal pattern while a muted trumpet comments in short, nocturnal punctuation.
tracks.groove: Slow bossa-inflected jazz pulse, featherlight and flexible rather than dance-driven.
tracks.harmony: Minor-key ii–V colors, lush major-seventh side steps, and deceptive cadences that avoid emphatic arrival.
tracks.development: Guitar establishes the pulse, piano fills the upper space, trumpet enters with clipped motifs, the texture briefly becomes more conversational, then returns to guitar and bass.

tracks.title: A Door Left Ajar
tracks.musicalRole: Tenor saxophone sustains a single evolving melody over a pedal bass, with piano changing the surrounding harmonic light.
tracks.groove: Sparse, slow swing with the bass repeating a calm two-note figure and drums entering only at phrase turns.
tracks.harmony: Long pedal-point foundation supporting shifting upper triads, suspended dominants, and occasional blues inflections.
tracks.development: Open with bass pedal and piano voicing, introduce the sax melody in long breaths, gradually ornament its returns, then let the melody fragment while the pedal remains unresolved.

tracks.title: Underpass Lullaby
tracks.musicalRole: A small ensemble alternates between a low, repeating bass figure and a fragile flute melody, using silence as the main transition.
tracks.groove: Slow 5/4 grouped gently as 2+3, with the asymmetry felt as a lilt rather than a puzzle.
tracks.harmony: Revolving minor ninth sonorities and chromatic bass approaches, with occasional open fifths to release density.
tracks.development: Bass establishes the uneven lullaby, electric piano adds sparse color, flute enters in short phrases, the middle doubles the motif in wider register, and the ending leaves only bass harmonics and air.

tracks.title: Afterimage in Brass
tracks.musicalRole: Muted trombone and piano trade broad phrases while bass and brushes maintain a soft, nearly motionless foundation.
tracks.groove: Very slow 4/4 with spacious swing and occasional held bars that suspend forward motion.
tracks.harmony: Chromatic descending inner voices beneath stable roots, moving between minor, dominant-sus, and ambiguous major sonorities.
tracks.development: Piano presents the harmonic frame, trombone enters with a wide descending line, the exchange becomes denser without getting louder, then both instruments converge on a quiet open interval.

tracks.title: Dawn Without Arrival
tracks.musicalRole: A restrained quintet gradually transforms a simple piano motif from shadowed minor into softened, unresolved brightness.
tracks.groove: Slow, floating swing that becomes increasingly sparse near the end.
tracks.harmony: Begins with minor ninth and suspended colors, introduces relative-major inflections, then avoids a full cadence through common-tone voicings.
tracks.development: Piano states the motif, bass and brushes establish a barely moving bed, flugelhorn lengthens the melody, vibraphone adds a late halo, and the ensemble recedes into a final common tone.
